message.content:
`docker start` is **not** the command to bring up the Docker daemon – it’s used to start *containers* that were previously stopped. On Windows the Docker Engine runs as a Windows Service (or as part of Docker Desktop). To get the Docker daemon running you need to start that service, not call `docker start`. ### How to start the Docker daemon/service | Method | Command | Notes | |--------|---------|-------| | **PowerShell (recommended)** | ```powershell
Start-Service -Name com.docker.service
``` | Requires administrative rights. Checks status automatically. | | **Command Prompt / CMD** | ```cmd
sc start com.docker.service
``` | Same effect as PowerShell but uses the native `sc` utility. | | **Docker Desktop GUI** | Double‑click the Docker Desktop icon from the Start Menu or taskbar. | This will launch the Docker Desktop app which in turn starts the underlying service. | If you’re using Docker Desktop, simply opening the application is usually enough – it will start the background service for you. If you’re working on a headless server or a custom installation, use one of the service‑starting commands above. --- #### Quick sanity check After starting the service, verify that Docker is ready: ```bash docker version ``` You should see client and server versions printed without errors. If you still get “Cannot connect to the Docker daemon”, double‑check that the service name matches your installation (`com.docker.service` is the default for Docker Desktop). --- **Bottom line:** Use `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` (or `sc start com.docker.service`) to start the Docker daemon on Windows. `docker start` only starts existing containers.
